Re: Appeal of Prior Authorization Denial  
Member: Quinn Grant  
Member ID: W553544386  
Plan: UnitedHealthcare Commercial/ACA, Minnesota  
Reference number: POC-87E365CAED-66145  
Requested service: ACL reconstruction  
CPT: 29888  
Ordering surgeon: Duval, MD  

Dear UnitedHealthcare Appeals Reviewer:

I am appealing the denial of prior authorization for ACL reconstruction, CPT 29888. The denial states that the submitted records did not document an adequate trial of conservative treatment. The clinical records do document extensive conservative treatment, with persistent symptoms and objective findings despite that treatment.

I have had 24 months of progressive knee pain that has not resolved with rest. I completed 10 weeks of supervised physical therapy from April 12, 2026, through June 21, 2026, including 20 visits. Therapy addressed range of motion and quadriceps strengthening, and treatment also included bracing. The physical therapy discharge note documents completion of this course.

Additional conservative treatment has also failed to provide adequate relief:

- NSAID treatment was used for six months with inadequate relief.
- A corticosteroid injection on April 17, 2026, produced only three weeks of partial relief.
- Rest and bracing did not resolve the pain or instability.

The records also establish a structural cause for the ongoing symptoms. MRI performed on June 29, 2026, demonstrated a complete mid-substance tear of the anterior cruciate ligament with a bone-bruise pattern. The menisci were intact, and there was no significant arthritis. Clinically, I have recurrent instability with pivoting and have experienced two episodes of giving way on stairs. Examination showed positive provocative testing on the affected side, with range of motion limited by pain.

These findings show that the requested reconstruction is not being pursued before conservative care. Rather, conservative care has been completed and has not adequately relieved the symptoms or prevented recurrent instability. The MRI-confirmed complete ACL tear, recurrent giving-way episodes, persistent pain, and abnormal examination support the medical necessity of reconstruction.

The records also document the absence of complicating factors that would otherwise interfere with treatment: there is no active infection, no untreated substance use, and the patient is a nonsmoker. BMI is 29.

Please overturn the denial and approve prior authorization for ACL reconstruction, CPT 29888, by Duval, MD. If UnitedHealthcare maintains the denial, please provide the complete clinical criteria and review guidelines actually applied to this request, identify the specific records or requirements considered insufficient, and provide the clinical rationale for concluding that the documented 10-week, 20-visit supervised physical therapy course, bracing, six months of NSAIDs, injection treatment, and continued instability did not satisfy the conservative-treatment requirement.

The public policy document has not been quoted in this appeal because its full text was not available for reliable extraction. This appeal is based on the denial reason and the clinical records summarized above.

Please confirm receipt of this appeal and provide the appeal determination in writing.

Sincerely,

Quinn Grant
